jobs.description:
About ClearGov 

 ClearGov is building the modern financial operating layer for the public sector. 

 We help US local governments and school districts plan, budget, report, and communicate their finances with clarity and confidence. From long-term planning to financial reporting, compliance, and transparency, our platform connects the work finance teams are already doing and makes it easier to deliver for their communities. 

Today, more than 2,000 public sector organizations use ClearGov, and we continue to expand our platform and reach as we grow.

 Our Core Values 

 Be Clear & Credible  

 We are authentic in our interactions, communicating with clarity, speaking with honesty, and following through with consistency. We turn transparency into our greatest competitive advantage. 

 Be Human   

 We are human partners to our colleagues and customers and lead with consideration and kindness - making space for others to do the same. We turn empathy into a shared strength.

 Be Better Together   

 We are committed to building an inclusive community where everyone thrives. We share successes, support each other through challenges, and show up for our teammates the way we show up for our customers. We turn togetherness into our greatest advantage and collaboration into our greatest multiplier.

 Be Honourable/Honorable   

 We are responsible to our colleagues and customers. We bring our full selves to every conversation, every project, every decision, and every relationship. We act with intention, deliver on our commitments, and lead with integrity - even when no one is watching. We turn honour into the foundation that powers everything we do.

 Be Connected 

 We are culture builders where people are seen, welcomed, and celebrated. We show up in every interaction - the laughs, the wins, the hard days. We turn connection into opportunities for people to feel they belong.

 What Makes You a Great Fit 

 You take ownership and follow through

 You communicate clearly and effectively

 You're comfortable solving problems and figuring things out

 You learn quickly and adapt as things change

 You care about the team, not just your own work

 You bring a sense of humor and perspective to what you do

 About the Opportunity 

 ClearGov has built a strong product marketing foundation, with an established team supporting product launches, messaging, and sales enablement across a growing portfolio. As the company enters its next phase of growth, ClearGov is hiring a Director of Product & Solution Marketing to elevate the function from strong product-level execution to platform-and- solution-level strategy.

 Reporting to the VP of Marketing, this leader will define how ClearGov positions, packages, and brings to market a suite of 13 products across cities, counties, school districts, and special districts, each with distinct needs and buying dynamics. The Director of Product & Solution Marketing will help the company make sharper decisions about where to invest, how the products fit together, and how ClearGov expands within its customer base.

 This is a highly visible leadership role with meaningful autonomy and direct access to the executive team and board. The Director of Product & Solution Marketing will serve as a strategic partner to the VP of Marketing, CPO and CRO, translating customer and market insight into portfolio choices and measurable commercial impact.

 This leader will manage an established team of four, creating a five-person product & solution marketing organization, with the opportunity to grow the team as the function expands.

 Key Responsibilities: 

 Lead pricing and packaging strategy: Set the strategic direction for bundling, discounting, and launch pricing in partnership with Product, Finance, Revenue, and external research partners.

 Set portfolio and commercialization strategy: Define how ClearGov’s products fit together, where bundling and cross-sell opportunities exist, and how positioning and go-to-market motions should vary across customer segments.

 Shape executive decision-making: Represent product marketing with the executive team and board, connecting market, customer, and competitive insight to growth priorities and business performance.

 Lead and develop the product marketing organization: Build on the team’s subject matter expertise and strengths in messaging, launches, and enablement while expanding its capabilities in portfolio strategy, market intelligence, pricing, and commercial planning.

 Build a scalable launch and integration model: Partner with Product, Marketing, and Sales on new product / bundle launches and create repeatable approaches for positioning, packaging, and commercializing acquired products.

 Strengthen expansion motions: Partner with Revenue and Marketing leaders to improve cross-sell, upsell, and account-based growth programs across ClearGov’s customer base.

 Establish a market and customer intelligence discipline: Build competitive intelligence, win-loss analysis, and industry engagement that inform product, sales, and portfolio decisions.

 Own the market narrative and field adoption: Craft bold, outcome-based messaging that clearly differentiates ClearGov from spreadsheets and competing vendors, including sharp depositioning that sales can use in live deals. Ensure sales actually uses what the team builds by measuring content adoption, retiring assets that go unused, and tying messaging to win rates.

 Create clear measures of impact: Define how product marketing performance is evaluated and connect the team’s work to adoption, expansion, win rates, and revenue outcomes.

 Critical Skills/Experience: 

 Significant product marketing leadership experience in B2B SaaS, including recent experience at the Director or Senior Director level, or operating at a comparable scope.

 Experience owning go-to-market or commercialization strategy across a multi-product / platform portfolio, multiple customer segments, or distinct buyer personas.

 Pricing and packaging experience, including bundling, discounting, or launch pricing.

 A track record of translating customer, market, and competitive insight into positioning, portfolio, investment, or growth decisions.

 People leadership experience, including building, developing, and elevating a product marketing team.

 Strong partnership with Product, Sales, and Marketing leaders in a mid-market or enterprise sales environment.

 Executive presence and sound judgment, with the ability to operate autonomously, align senior stakeholders, and communicate strategy clearly to executives and board members.

 Comfort operating in a growing, evolving business where portfolio priorities and organizational needs continue to change.

 Experience with mid-market or lower-enterprise B2B SaaS products in the $30K–$60K ARR range and sales cycles of approximately three to four months.

 Preferred Skills/Experience: 

 Experience with programmatic growth motions such as account-based marketing, cross-sell, or upsell at scale.

 Experience with enterprise SaaS products of $75k-$250M+

 Background in GovTech, FinTech, finance, accounting, compliance, or another technical or regulated vertical.

 Experience supporting growth through M&A, portfolio expansion, or product-line integration.

 Experience building win-loss, competitive intelligence, or industry analyst programs.

 Compensation: 

 In the spirit of transparency, we are excited to share the base salary for this position is $165,000 - $200,000 USD or $155,000 - 190,000 CAD, and exclusive of fringe benefits or potential bonuses. If you are hired at ClearGov, your final base salary compensation will be determined by factors such as skills, interview performance, education and/or experience. In addition to those factors, we believe in the importance of pay equity and consider internal equity of our current team members as a part of any final offer. Please keep in mind that the range mentioned above is the full base salary for the role. Hiring beyond the base range would not be typical in order to allow for future & continued salary growth. We also offer a generous compensation and benefits package (more information on benefits listed below).

 Why Join ClearGov 

 Remote and flexible work environment

 Meaningful work that impacts communities across the United States

 Collaborative, high-performing team

 Competitive compensation and benefits

 Opportunities to grow as we scale 

 Benefits 

 Medical, dental & vision insurance

 FSA, HSA, and/or Dependent Care FSA (US)

 Life + AD&D insurance, plus short-term and long-term disability insurance (US)

 Life + disability insurance (Canada)

 401(k) (US) / RRSP (Canada) with 3.5% match

 10 company holidays

 3 wellness days

 Paid vacation time off

 Sick and safe time off

 Paid parental leave

 Paid bereavement leave

 Paid jury duty + civic service leave

 Employee assistance program

 2 summer days + annual end-of-year "Dimming of the Lights"

 Employee referral bonus program

 How to Apply 
Ready to join us? Apply online today! 

 Equal Opportunity Employer 
ClearGov is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, age, or any other protected characteristic. Hiring decisions are based solely on qualifications, merit, and business needs.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation
jobs.description:
JOB PURPOSE 
 Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation leads the development and execution of the organization’s enterprise AI strategy and transformation agenda to drive measurable business value, productivity, operational efficiency, innovation, and informed decision-making. The role serves as the organization’s AI subject matter expert and enterprise coordinating point, providing strategic guidance on AI opportunities, investments, governance, risk, technology, adoption, and value realization. 

 The Director partners with business and functional leaders to identify, prioritize, and implement AI and intelligent automation opportunities aligned with organizational objectives and financial goals. The role initially focuses on leveraging AI to enhance financial and operational performance, including forecasting, reporting, analysis, productivity, workflow efficiency, cost management, and decision-making, with successful capabilities and practices progressively expanded across other functions. The Director oversees the enterprise AI portfolio and lifecycle from opportunity assessment and business case development through solution selection, implementation, adoption, benefits realization, ongoing monitoring, and retirement. 

 KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
 AI Strategy, Portfolio & Value Management Develop and maintain the enterprise AI strategy, operating model, portfolio, and roadmap aligned with corporate objectives and financial goals. 
 Identify, evaluate, and prioritize AI opportunities based on strategic alignment, business value, cost, complexity, data readiness, risk, and organizational readiness. 
 Develop business cases, investment recommendations, and implementation roadmaps, including build, buy, configure, or partner options. 
 Establish performance measures, baseline metrics, and value-realization frameworks to track AI adoption, ROI, productivity, cost savings, revenue impact, and other business outcomes. 
 Provide executive leadership with visibility into AI investments, performance, realized benefits, opportunities, and risks. 
 AI Solution Development & Implementation Lead the evaluation, design, development, and deployment of AI solutions across enterprise productivity, function-specific applications, intelligent automation, advanced AI, and emerging agentic capabilities. 
 Partner with business units and end users to identify opportunities, develop practical AI-enabled solutions, and improve processes and ways of working. 
 Oversee AI pilots, proofs of concept, and enterprise implementations through the full lifecycle—from opportunity identification and feasibility through deployment, adoption, benefits realization, monitoring, and retirement. 
 Coordinate with Cybersecurity, Human Resources and other stakeholders to ensure solutions are appropriately designed, implemented, adopted, and measured. 
 Assess solution performance and recommend whether initiatives should be scaled, enhanced, consolidated, paused, or retired based on business value, adoption, cost, and risk. 
 AI Governance, Risk & Responsible Adoption Establish and maintain enterprise AI governance frameworks, policies, standards, controls, and risk-based processes to support responsible AI adoption. 
 Ensure AI initiatives are appropriately assessed for cybersecurity, privacy, data, intellectual property, legal, ethical, third-party, model, and business continuity risks. 
 Maintain an enterprise inventory of approved AI technologies, platforms, models, agents, and material use cases, with appropriate review, approval, testing, human oversight, monitoring, and escalation requirements. 
 Ensure data quality, classification, access, security, information governance, and regulatory requirements are addressed before AI solutions are deployed. 
 Monitor the evolving AI landscape, regulatory expectations, and associated risks, and update governance practices as required. 
 Enterprise AI Adoption & Change Management Lead enterprise AI literacy, adoption, and change-management initiatives across executives, leaders, employees, technical teams, and advanced AI users. 
 Develop and deliver role- and function-specific training, guidance, and resources to promote effective and responsible use of AI. 
 Serve as the enterprise resource for AI strategy, best practices, use-case guidance, and adoption support. 
 Measure AI utilization, adoption, training effectiveness, employee feedback, and business outcomes to continuously improve AI enablement. 
 Coordinate internal subject matter experts, technology teams, business stakeholders, and external partners to support successful AI adoption 
 Vendor, Technology & Partner Management Evaluate AI technologies, vendors, consultants, platforms, and implementation partners against business requirements, value, security, architecture, scalability, risk, and total cost of ownership. 
 Manage AI technology and vendor relationships to ensure service quality, effective implementation, and value realization. 
 Maintain oversight of the enterprise AI technology portfolio to identify duplicate capabilities, unnecessary licensing, overlapping solutions, and opportunities for consolidation. 
 Monitor emerging AI technologies—including generative AI, large language models, predictive AI, intelligent automation, computer vision, and agentic AI—and assess their practical business applicability and potential value. 
 QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS, AND EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS 
  Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred. 
 Minimum seven (7) years of progressive experience in AI, data analytics, digital transformation, automation, technology, or related fields, including significant experience leading enterprise AI or generative AI adoption. 
 Proven experience leading complex, enterprise-wide AI or business transformation initiatives from strategy and business case development through implementation, adoption, scaling, and measurable value realization. 
 Strong business and financial acumen, including experience with budgeting, forecasting, reporting, business case development, technology investment evaluation, performance measurement, and ROI. 
 Strong knowledge of AI technologies, including generative AI, machine learning, predictive analytics, intelligent automation, large language models, AI agents, and emerging AI capabilities, with an understanding of data, cybersecurity, privacy, and AI governance. 
 Strong strategic thinking, analytical, communication, stakeholder management, project management, and change management skills, with the ability to translate complex technology into practical business solutions and influence cross-functional decisions.  
 Strong technical and business judgment to evaluate AI solutions, vendors, risks, data and technology dependencies, and investment decisions. Professional certifications in AI, analytics, project management, responsible AI, or AI governance are considered an asset. 

 PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORKING CONDITIONS Standard office setting - hybrid arrangement (4 days in-office) 
 Fast paced office environment 
 Travel expectations between facilities in Mississauga and North York

strategic financial executive to serve as its next Vice 
President, Finance and Administration / Chief Financial Officer.

leadership, strategic direction, and institutional stewardship

public safety, and facilities.

This position ensures the responsible management of 
institutional resources while advancing the school's mission, 
vision, and strategic priorities. Serving as a trusted advisor

provides sound financial counsel, and partners with executive 
leadership to maintain the school's fiscal strength, operational 
effectiveness, and long-term sustainability.

perspective and contribute to college-wide initiatives, 
organizational culture, governance, strategic planning, and 
executive decision-making.

first and functional leaders second. As members of the 
President’s Cabinet, they share responsibility for advancing the 
school's mission through collaborative leadership, strategic 
planning, innovation, and responsible stewardship of public 
resources.

The CFO will balance financial discipline with innovation, 
operational excellence with exceptional customer service, and 
long-term sustainability with the evolving needs of students, 
employees, and the community.

Success will be measured not only by the performance of assigned 
departments, but also by meaningful contributions to the overall 
effectiveness, reputation, and future of the college.

 Cabinet and Strategic Leadership

executive leadership team.

• Advise the President on strategic, financial, operational, and 
organizational matters.

• Participate in institutional planning, executive 
decision-making, and policy development.

• Collaborate across divisions to advance college-wide 
initiatives and strategic priorities.

• Represent the school before governmental agencies, financial 
institutions, professional organizations, and community 
partners.

• Develop long-range financial and operational strategies that 
support the school’s Strategic Plan.

• Evaluate emerging trends, risks, and opportunities affecting 
higher education and public finance.

• Champion innovation, continuous improvement, and responsible 
resource management.

 Organizational Leadership 

• Recruit, develop, mentor, and evaluate executive leaders and

jobs.description:
About Modern Campus 
 Modern Campus empowers institutions to move with confidence across the modern learner journey. Our platform spans web content management, curriculum and catalog management, student engagement and lifelong learning — giving more than 1,700 colleges and universities the infrastructure they need to support the entire learner-to-earner lifecycle and deliver personalized, scalable experiences. 

  We partner with the education community to create new pathways for learning and opportunity, reimagining how institutions serve the modern learner and shape the future of education. 

 Our purpose — our north star — is to empower institutions to confidently serve and support the modern learner. 

  This mission and purpose come to life through how we show up every day: 
 We exist to create empowerment through education. 
 We lead with honesty and empathy. 
 We shape the future through innovation. 
 We become trusted partners. 
 We make the complex feel possible. Position Summary 
 Modern Campus is seeking a visionary and execution-oriented Vice President, Product Innovation to identify, validate, build, and scale new product opportunities while transforming how we develop products through AI-enabled and agentic practices. 

 This leader will serve as the company's innovation catalyst, balancing customer discovery, strategic product incubation, and organizational transformation. The Vice President, Product Innovation will lead the creation of new offerings that expand our portfolio while establishing scalable, AI-native product development capabilities that accelerate speed, quality, and customer value across the organization. 

 The role partners closely with Product Management, Engineering, Design, Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, and Executive Leadership to drive growth through both new products and new ways of building products. 
 What You'll Do 
 Product Innovation & New Venture Development 
 Identify, validate, and launch innovative software products that address emerging challenges and opportunities in higher education. 
 Lead customer discovery, market research, and rapid experimentation to assess new market opportunities. 
 Build and test MVPs, prototypes, and pilot programs to validate customer demand and commercial viability. 
 Define business models, pricing strategies, and go-to-market approaches for new offerings. 
 Partner with Product, Engineering, Design, Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success teams to successfully transition validated concepts into scalable businesses. 
 Develop and manage an innovation portfolio that balances incremental improvements with transformative growth opportunities. 
 Foster a culture of experimentation, learning, and innovation across the product organization. 
 AI-Enabled Product Development Leadership 
 Define and champion Modern Campus's vision for AI-enabled and agentic product development. 
 Establish best practices for leveraging AI across the product lifecycle, including customer research, discovery, requirements gathering, prototyping, documentation, testing, experimentation, and product operations. 
 Evaluate emerging AI technologies and identify opportunities to improve how product teams operate and deliver value. 
 Develop repeatable frameworks, playbooks, governance models, and adoption strategies for responsible AI implementation. 
 Partner with Product, Engineering, and Design leaders to embed AI-native practices into day-to-day product development workflows. 
 Measure and continuously improve the impact of AI-enabled practices on customer outcomes, delivery speed, and organizational effectiveness. 
 Promote a culture of experimentation, continuous learning, and responsible AI adoption across the company. 
 Executive Leadership & Collaboration 
 Influence company strategy through innovation insights, customer feedback, and emerging market opportunities. 
 Communicate vision, strategy, business cases, and outcomes effectively to executive leadership and key stakeholders. 
 Build alignment across departments to accelerate innovation initiatives and organizational transformation. 
 Serve as a thought leader on AI, product innovation, and emerging technology trends. 
 What You'll Bring 
 Required Qualifications 
 Proven experience leading software products from concept through customer validation, commercial launch, and post-launch scaling. 
 Experience building and managing innovation portfolios, product incubators, or venture-style product development initiatives. 
 Demonstrated success delivering revenue-generating software products, including business model development, pricing strategy, and go-to-market execution. 
 Deep understanding of artificial intelligence technologies and their application to software product development. 
 Hands-on experience leveraging AI tools and agentic workflows to accelerate product development and decision-making. 
 Strong executive presence and communication skills with the ability to influence strategy and organizational change. 
 Proven ability to operate effectively in fast-paced, ambiguous, and rapidly evolving environments. 
 10+ years of progressive product leadership experience within a software organization. 
 Experience leading cross-functional teams, major product launches, and strategic initiatives. 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 MBA or advanced business degree. 
 Experience in higher education, education technology, SaaS, or other complex B2B software markets. 
 Experience scaling AI-enabled product organizations. 
 Track record of launching net-new businesses, platforms, or product categories. 
 Success in This Role 
 Within the first 12–24 months, successful outcomes may include: 
 Launching three or more new product experiments into market. 
 Creating a repeatable and measurable innovation pipeline from idea to commercialization. 
 Generating meaningful new revenue streams from newly launched offerings. 
 Increasing product team effectiveness through AI-enabled workflows and agentic development practices. 
 Improving speed-to-market and customer value realization across the product portfolio. 
 Establishing Modern Campus as a leader in AI-enabled product innovation within higher education technology. 
 Why Join Modern Campus? 
 At Modern Campus, we're transforming how higher education institutions engage learners throughout the entire student lifecycle. We believe meaningful growth comes from understanding our customers, connecting their challenges to the right solutions, and creating experiences that deliver measurable value. 
 This role offers an opportunity to shape the future of demand generation at Modern Campus, building innovative, data-driven marketing strategies that strengthen customer engagement, accelerate growth, and connect marketing impact to business outcomes.

jobs.title: Director, Sales Operations (Corporate)
jobs.location: 3737 Thimens Blvd, Montreal (Saint-Laurent), Quebec, Canada; 111 Progress, Scarborough, Ontario, Canada
jobs.description:
“Join us in building Careers and shaping Experiences Beyond the Box”   

 About Us 

 At Atlantic Packaging, every box tells a story and yours begins here. As a proudly Canadian-owned company with over 80 years of excellence in the corrugated packaging industry with operations within North America (Ontario, Quebec and United States), we’re committed to sustainability, customer excellence and community impact. Since 1945, we’ve supported local jobs and built a legacy of trust with our clients and team members. At Atlantic, your ideas matter, your growth is supported and your work makes a real impact.

 The Opportunity 

 The Director, Sales Operations is responsible for owning, standardizing, and continuously improving the commercial operating system across the organization. This is a corporate role working in collaboration with all sales regions in the Atlantic Packaging network (Ontario, Quebec, USA).

 This role does not own sales targets nor manage sales teams directly. Instead, it enables Sales Leadership and P&L owners to execute consistently by providing clear processes, disciplined governance, and effective tools.

 The role addresses recurring structural issues in sales execution (contracts, risk exposure, forecast visibility, onboarding effectiveness, and CRM adoption) and brings process excellence to an area historically driven by individual experience rather than system discipline. Sales Operations builds the system so Sales / Marketing / Legal / Finance / CX work together efficiently.

 The corporate Customer Experience function will report into the Director, Sales Operations, which expect will increase the probability that customer feedback results in retention, growth, and operational improvement.

 Success Factors in the Role 

 Success in this role will be judged on system outcomes, not activity.

 Sales execution becomes repeatable

 Fewer deal-specific workarounds; consistent deal flow through the same stages and approvals.

 Sales leaders use the tools willingly

 Salesforce is used because it makes running the business easier, not because it’s mandated.

 Commercial risks are visible before decisions (with a disciplined reduction process)

 P&L owners can see contract duration mix, terms exposure, and liability accumulation before approving deals.

 Fewer “surprises”

 Fewer last-minute escalations due to undocumented terms, unclear approvals, or cross‑region inconsistencies.

 Improved funnel credibility

 Forecast discussions are grounded in a shared, disciplined view of the pipeline.

 CX feedback loop is integrated into the sales process which will result in better CX scores across the businesses

 What You’ll Do 

 This role sets standards and runs governance. Sales Leadership owns execution. Finance/Credit/Legal co-own approval rules and risk thresholds.

 1. Sales Operating Model & Governance

 Own and maintain the front-end sales operating model, including:

 Contract approval workflows and limits of authority (with Legal).

 Clear rules when customers operate across regions.

 Partner with Legal, Finance, and Credit to make risk explicit and decision-ready.

 Ensure P&L leaders have visibility before commitments are made, not after.

 2. Salesforce Ownership

 Act as business owner of Salesforce (process design, usage standards, reporting logic).

 Drive adoption by defining how and why Salesforce is used:

 Funnel structure aligned with business needs (product mix, seasonality, capacity).

 Standard dashboards for P&L owners and Sales Leadership.

 Reduce “system noise” so the tool supports decisions, not administration.

 3. Funnel Management & Sales Planning

 Define and enforce consistent funnel management practices.

 Provide forward-looking visibility on revenue concentration by:

 Factory

 Asset type

 Industry

 Salesperson

 Other cuts as needed

 Enable proactive capacity and production discussions (vs. reactive firefighting).

 Drive development of sales plans that can be handed off for execution.

 Enable consolidation of this data for the Group.

 4. Contract, Terms & Risk Tracking

 Implement standardized reporting on:

 Contract tenure mix (no contract, quarterly, annual, etc.).

 Payment terms exposure.

 Aggregate liability commitments.

 Make commercial risk measured, visible, and discussable (not implicit or anecdotal).

 5. Sales Training / Motivation / Sales incentive management

 Design and institutionalize a formal sales onboarding and training framework.

 Develop role-specific training (e.g., Salesforce usage, contract basics).

 Build a repeatable cadence for sales meetings to drive consistent themes and execution.

 Administer the sales incentive program, including consistent publishing of performance vs. targets.

 6. Manage corporate CX program

 What You Bring 

 Strong background in Sales Operations, Commercial Excellence, or Revenue Enablement.

 Must be fluent in both French/English 

 Comfortable influencing senior sales leaders without hierarchical authority.

 Process-oriented, systems thinker with a strong business bias.

 Credible with Finance, Sales, and Operations alike.

 Required: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Commerce, Finance, Operations, or a related field required.

 7+ years of experience in progressive experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Commercial Excellence, or Business Analytics

 Expert in Salesforce, specifically in design, governance and adoption.

  What We Offer 

 Comprehensive health, dental and vision coverage (dependents included)

 Teamwork-focused culture with sustainability initiatives and social events

 A culture of appreciation through a point-based recognition

 Opportunities for advancement and internal movement

 Education assistance for continuous skill development

 Academic scholarships for employees’ children

 Safety equipment and PPE support program

 Retirement savings and wellness initiatives

 Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

 Inclusion and Accessibility 

 Atlantic Packaging is committed to fostering an inclusive, accessible and respectful environment for all candidates. If you require accommodation during the hiring process, please contact our Talent Acquisition team—we’re here to support you.

 We sincerely thank all applicants for their interest in joining Atlantic Packaging. While we appreciate the time and effort invested, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

 Please Note:
Candidates who are 18 years or older are required to complete a criminal and background check. Details will be provided through the application process.

 Sommaire du rôle 

 Le/La Directeur(trice), opérations commerciales corporatives est responsable de définir, standardiser et améliorer en continu le système d’exploitation commercial de l’organisation. Il s’agit d’un rôle corporatif qui travaille en collaboration avec toutes les régions de ventes du réseau Atlantic Packaging, incluant l’Ontario, le Québec et les États-Unis.

 Ce rôle n’est pas propriétaire des objectifs de ventes et ne gère pas directement les équipes de ventes. Son rôle est plutôt de permettre aux leaders des ventes et aux responsables P&L d’exécuter de façon constante, en mettant en place des processus clairs, une gouvernance disciplinée et des outils efficaces.

 Le rôle adresse des enjeux structurels récurrents dans l’exécution commerciale, notamment les contrats, l’exposition aux risques, la visibilité sur le funnel, l’efficacité de l’intégration des nouveaux employés et l’adoption de Salesforce. Il amène de la rigueur de processus dans une fonction qui a historiquement reposé davantage sur l’expérience individuelle que sur une discipline institutionnelle. Les opérations commerciales corporatives bâtissent le système pour permettre aux Ventes / Marketing / Légal / Finances / CX de travailler ensemble efficacement.

 La fonction corporative d’expérience client relèvera du/de la Directeur(trice), opérations commerciales corporatives, ce qui est un arrimage naturel puisque la Voix du client, l’adoption de Salesforce, la discipline du funnel, la boucle fermée et les cadences commerciales doivent être connectées au même système de gestion pour transformer les commentaires clients en actions concrètes, soutenir la rétention, favoriser la croissance et améliorer l’exécution opérationnelle.

 Facteurs de succès dans le rôle 

 Le succès dans ce rôle sera évalué sur les résultats du système, et non sur le niveau d’activité.

 L’exécution des ventes devient reproductible

 Moins d’exceptions gérées à la pièce; un flux de dossiers plus constant à travers les mêmes étapes et approbations.

 Les leaders des ventes utilisent les outils parce qu’ils les aident à gérer le business

 Salesforce est utilisé parce qu’il facilite la gestion commerciale, et non seulement parce qu’il est obligatoire.

 Les risques commerciaux sont visibles avant les décisions

 Les responsables P&L peuvent voir la durée des contrats, l’exposition aux termes de paiement et les engagements de responsabilité avant d’approuver les ententes.

 Moins de surprises

 Moins d’escalades de dernière minute causées par des termes non documentés, des approbations floues ou des incohérences entre régions.

 Crédibilité accrue du funnel

 Les discussions de prévisions sont basées sur une vision partagée et disciplinée du pipeline.

 La boucle de rétroaction CX est intégrée au processus de ventes afin d’améliorer les scores CX dans l’ensemble des unités d’affaires.

 Portée et responsabilités clés 

 Ce rôle établit les standards et anime la gouvernance. Les leaders des ventes demeurent propriétaires de l’exécution. Les finances, le crédit et le légal codéfinissent les règles d’approbation et les seuils de risque.

 1. Modèle opérationnel des ventes et gouvernance

 Définir et maintenir le modèle opérationnel commercial de première ligne, incluant les flux d’approbation des contrats, les limites d’autorité et les règles applicables aux clients opérant dans plusieurs régions.

 Travailler avec le juridique, les finances et le crédit afin de rendre le risque explicite et prêt à être décidé.

 S’assurer que les leaders P&L ont la visibilité requise avant que les engagements soient pris, et non après.

 2. Ownership Salesforce

 Agir comme propriétaire d’affaires de Salesforce pour le design des processus, les standards d’utilisation et la logique de reporting.

 Favoriser l’adoption en définissant clairement comment et pourquoi Salesforce est utilisé.

 Aligner la structure du funnel avec les besoins d’affaires, incluant le mix produit, la saisonnalité et la capacité.

 Développer des tableaux de bord standards pour les responsables P&L et les leaders des ventes.

 Réduire le bruit administratif afin que l’outil soutienne les décisions, plutôt que de devenir une couche de reporting additionnelle.

 3. Gestion du funnel et planification des ventes

 Définir et faire vivre des pratiques cohérentes à travers le groupe de gestion du funnel.

 Donner une visibilité prospective sur la concentration des revenus par usine, type d’actif, industrie, représentant et autres découpages nécessaires.

 Permettre des discussions proactives sur la capacité et la production, plutôt que de fonctionner en mode réaction ou escalade.

 Contribuer au développement de plans de ventes clairs, prêts à être transférés en exécution.

 Permettre une consolidation au niveau du groupe de ces données.

 4. Contrats, termes et suivi des risques

 Mettre en place un reporting standardisé sur la durée des contrats, l’exposition aux termes de paiement et les engagements de responsabilité.

 Rendre le risque commercial mesurable, visible et discutable, plutôt qu’implicite ou anecdotique.

 5. Formation, mobilisation et gestion des incitatifs de ventes

 Concevoir et institutionnaliser un cadre formel d’intégration et de formation pour les équipes de ventes.

 Développer des formations adaptées aux rôles, notamment sur Salesforce et les notions de base liées aux contrats.

 Bâtir une cadence reproductible pour les rencontres de ventes afin de renforcer les thèmes clés et l’exécution.

 Administrer le programme d’incitatifs de ventes, incluant la publication constante de la performance par rapport aux objectifs.

 6. Gestion du programme corporatif d’expérience client

 Assurer l’arrimage entre la Voix du client, les données d’expérience client, Salesforce, les initiatives de ventes et les priorités opérationnelles.

 Mettre en place une boucle fermée permettant de transformer les commentaires, irritants et opportunités d’amélioration provenant des clients en actions concrètes, priorisées et mesurables.

 Renforcer la culture client en rendant les enjeux CX visibles, actionnables et intégrés aux cadences commerciales et opérationnelles.

 Profil recherché 

 Solide expérience en opérations commerciales, excellence commerciale, enablement ou analytique commerciale.

 Capacité d’influencer des leaders de ventes expérimentés sans autorité hiérarchique directe.

 Profil structuré, orienté processus et système, avec une forte proximité d’affaires.

 Crédible auprès des ventes, des finances et des opérations.

 Formation et expérience 

 Baccalauréat requis en administration des affaires, commerce, finance, opérations ou domaine connexe.

 Doit maîtriser couramment le français et l’anglais.

 Minimum de 7 ans d’expérience progressive en opérations commerciales, revenue operations, excellence commerciale ou analytique d’affaires.

 Expertise avancée avec Salesforce, particulièrement en design, gouvernance et adoption.

VP, Digital Experience & Growth 

 Job Type: Full time
 Location: Toronto
 Reporting to: CEO
 Role Type: New

 Goway Travel was founded in Toronto in 1970 by Bruce Hodge, a young Australian economist who moved to Canada to follow his dreams.

 From there, we have established ourselves as a global influence with offices in Toronto, Vancouver, Los Angeles, Sydney, and Manila. While the travel industry endured major challenges, our strong foundations allowed Goway to forge ahead. We continually innovated, invested in new technology, and challenged the status quo.

 Still owned and operated by Bruce, with the support of his leadership board, our mission has always been to help our clients realize their travel dreams. Today, we are an industry-leading, global travel company with over 800 employees. Our team of experts utilizes cutting-edge technology to tailor-make 4 and 5-star travel experiences in over 100 countries around the world.

 At Goway Travel, we're not just a company; we're a family of dreamers and doers, inspired by our founder’s incredible journey. He didn't just follow a career path; he followed his heart, and in doing so, he built a company that helps others follow theirs.

 If you’re passionate about travel and innovation, we invite you to be a part of our exciting journey!

 Job Purpose:  

 As our first Vice President, Digital Experience & Growth, reporting directly to the CEO, you’ll own the digital growth engine end to end: the website, search, performance marketing, lifecycle, and the data that ties it all together.  If you thrive in an environment where innovation meets real-world impact, this role offers the opportunity to shape the technology behind unforgettable journeys. 

 What will be your key responsibilities? 

 Own the vision, governance and performance of Goway’s web properties and portals, leading CRO, UX, merchandising and customer-journey improvements.

 Shape strategy across paid, organic search, referral and emerging channels, tying investment to revenue, profitability, lead quality and long-term customer value.

 Build lifecycle strategy for Direct travellers and Trade partners, including journeys, nurture programs, re-engagement flows, advisor communications, personalization, loyalty, retention and referral.

 Build reporting that links marketing activity and website performance to business results, and partner with Technology on segmentation, audience strategy, lead-quality analysis and customer data strategy.

 Required Skills and Qualifications:  

 15+ years of progressive leadership in digital marketing, digital product, e-commerce, lifecycle, growth, CRM, analytics or customer experience.

 A track record of leading digital transformation or growth initiatives that moved the numbers.

 Hands-on strength in website optimization, SEO, acquisition, conversion, personalization and retention.

 Deep fluency in CRM, journey orchestration, marketing automation, analytics and martech, with the ability to lead across Marketing, Technology, Sales and Operations.

 What can you expect from Goway? 
Imagine working for a company where your career feels like an adventure. At Goway, you’ll join a global community that supports one another:

 We offer a competitive salary accompanied by performance incentives, and we place real importance on time away from work, such as paid personal days for when life calls for them and your birthday off each year.

 Your future matters to us, so we match your RRSP contributions and provide comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage.

 Our commitment to professional growth means you’ll have access to continuous learning and industry-leading training that keeps you at the forefront of travel innovation.

 Travel is in our DNA, so you’ll enjoy exclusive perks and discounts on worldwide getaways.

 Since we operate across Toronto, Vancouver, Los Angeles, Manila, Sydney, and beyond, you’ll collaborate across cultures and shape a career path that reflects your ambitions.

 Goway is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate differences and are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace for everyone. We appreciate every applicant’s interest. Please be advised that only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

Goway Travel Ltd will retain applications, notifications, and records related to this posting for three years, reflecting our commitment to fair and equitable hiring practices.

Please be aware of any suspicious emails or WhatsApp activity from individuals pretending to be recruiters or senior personnel at Goway Travel. We will never ask you to install an app during the recruitment process. If you receive a message of this nature, please ignore it and report it to Goway.

 About Goway 
Founded in Toronto in 1970 by Australian economist Bruce Hodge, Goway has evolved from a one-person dream into a family-owned global leader in tailor-made travel. With our headquarters in Toronto and hubs in Vancouver, Los Angeles, Sydney, and Manila, our team of over 700 talented employees designs travel experiences in more than 115 countries across all seven continents. We’re united by a passion for travel and are committed to doing the right thing: supporting diversity, equity, inclusion, and sustainable tourism that enriches local communities. Whether working remotely or side by side in one of our offices, we operate as one forward-thinking team, transforming wanderlust into life-changing adventures for our fellow Globetrotters. Director, Technical Operations (Platform) 

 Job Type: Permanent Full Time
 Location: Hybrid - Toronto, Ontario

 Job purpose 

 The Director, Technology Operations owns the operational health of the platforms Goway sells and services travel on: our reservations platform, the infrastructure it runs on, the supplier, air and distribution integrations it depends on, and the automation and data pipelines built around it.

 This is a practice-building role. You will define and own Goway's technical operations discipline: service levels, incident management, change control, observability and operational readiness, and you will make them the standard across our technology organisation. You will work alongside other Technology leaders. You will own the technology operations of our platform. You will have the CTO's mandate and backing to build the practice.

 What will be your key responsibilities? 

 Reliability and service management

 Define, publish and report service levels and service-level objectives for revenue-critical services, starting with quoting, booking, payment and traveller servicing.

 Own incident management end to end: severity definitions, escalation, incident command, communication during an incident, and post-incident review with corrective actions.

 Own RCA and problem management.

 Own change and release management as a company standard, balancing delivery throughput against change failure rate.

 Build observability sufficient to detect degradation.

 Own disaster recovery and business continuity for platform services, tested and documented on a stated cadence.

 Integration and supplier platform operations

 Monitoring of integration paths, error and failure-rate thresholds, and defined fallback behaviour when a partner degrades.

 Maintain a dependency map of the external platforms our revenue-generating flows rely on, with assessed operational risk and mitigation for each.

 Own operational readiness for new integrations and new product lines entering the platform.

 Own the operational reliability of automation and data pipelines in production.

 Platform and cloud operations

 Day-to-day operation of the AWS and managed hosting infrastructure serving our platform estate: environments, provisioning, patching and lifecycle management.

 Own hosting cost governance: visibility by service, a unit-cost measure, and an annual optimisation target.

 Lead capacity planning against forecast booking and travel volumes.

 Reduce manual, repeatable operational work through automation.

 Address seasonal capacity planning, change freezes and enhanced coverage aligned to our booking and departure peaks and to new product launches.

 Vendors, partners and compliance

 Platform, hosting and integration partner relationships: SLA definition, enforcement and structured performance review.

 Reduce single points of dependency, whether on a vendor or an individual.

 Partner with security on vulnerability management, patch compliance, access control and audit readiness.

 Report operational performance, risk and investment needs to the CTO and executive team in business terms.

 Ability to set standards and drive adoption across teams.

 Ability to communicate operational risk and performance.

 Preferred

jobs.title: Senior Director, Marketing & Communications
jobs.location: Dorval Head Office, Dorval, Quebec, Canada
jobs.description:
Founded in 2000 by three former Royal Canadian Air Force (RCAF) CF-18 fighter pilots who identified an opportunity to improve military readiness training, Top Aces has since established itself as the world leader in contracted adversary air (ADAIR) services and joint terminal attack controller (JTAC) training.

 We pride ourselves on our unblemished safety record, having flown an industry leading 160,000+ hours of operational training without accident in support of customers worldwide, including Canada, the U.S., Germany, and multiple other NATO allies and international partner nations.

 Our vision is to be the most trusted provider of innovative defense training solutions, continuously elevating standards in an industry where "Experience Matters." This commitment to innovation and technology ensures we remain adaptable, training allied militaries to succeed against evolving threats.

 Top Aces’ dynamic team contributes to delivering on our purpose of training the next generation of combat leaders by living our values of Service, Integrity, Excellence, and Together every day!

 Join our team!

 Position Summary 

 The Senior Director, Marketing & Communications is responsible for developing and leading Top Aces' marketing, brand, and communications strategy. The role leads a team of marketing and communications professionals and ensures that the company's messaging, brand presence, employee communications, and external profile support corporate priorities and business growth.

 The position also provides strategic oversight of government relations activities through the direction and management of external Government Relations advisors. The Senior Director establishes priorities, aligns advisor activities with business objectives, monitors performance, and coordinates internal support for advisor-led advocacy and stakeholder engagement initiatives. The role is not intended to execute day-to-day lobbying activities.

 The Senior Director serves as a trusted advisor to executive leadership on marketing, reputation, executive communications, media relations, employee communications, brand positioning, and strategic stakeholder engagement.

 Key Responsibilities 

 Marketing Strategy & Brand Management 

 Develop and execute a global marketing strategy for showcasing the company’s capabilities in line with corporate priorities, growth objectives, and business development needs.

 Lead brand positioning and ensure consistent use of approved brand standards across the business, regions, channels, and external materials.

 Oversee the development of marketing campaigns, presentations, digital content, videos, advertising, promotional materials, and customer-facing collateral.

 Lead the strategy for corporate events, trade shows, conferences, partnerships, and sponsorships.

 Partner with Business Development and executive leadership to support customer pursuits and strategic initiatives.

 Monitor market trends, audience insights, competitor activity, and emerging opportunities to strengthen positioning and campaign effectiveness.

 Internal Communications 

 Develop and execute an internal communications strategy that supports employee engagement, culture, organizational alignment, and change initiatives.

 Lead the preparation of executive messages, employee announcements, leadership updates, All Employee Calls, and communications for major corporate initiatives.

 Advise leaders on communication approaches for organizational changes and employee-facing initiatives.

 Measure the reach and effectiveness of internal communications and continuously improve channels and content.

 External Communications & Media Relations 

 Develop and implement an external communications strategy to strengthen Top Aces' visibility, credibility, and reputation.

 Lead the preparation of corporate messaging, press releases, media statements, website content, social media, corporate announcements, and executive communications.

 Lead media relations and manage relationships with relevant industry and business media.

 Support senior leaders with interviews, speeches, presentations, strategic messaging, and public-facing engagements.

 Lead crisis communications planning and coordinate communications responses during business-critical situations.

 Ensure consistent messaging across markets, audiences, and communication channels.

 Government Relations Agency Oversight 

 Establish annual Government Relations priorities in consultation with executive leadership, Strategy, and Business Development.

 Direct and manage external Government Relations advisors responsible for executing the company's Government Relations activities.

 Set clear advisor mandates, budgets, and reporting expectations.

 Review and approve advisor-developed stakeholder strategies, engagement plans, briefing materials, advocacy campaigns, and government-facing messaging.

 Coordinate internal subject-matter experts and executives to support agency-led government outreach and stakeholder meetings.

 Ensure Government Relations activities are aligned with business objectives, customer pursuits, corporate messaging, and reputation considerations.

 Monitor relevant government, defence, procurement, policy, and regulatory developments through agency reporting and other appropriate sources.

 Assess advisor performance, manage contracts and budgets, and recommend changes to external support where required.

 Ensure activities are conducted in accordance with applicable lobbying, transparency, ethics, and reporting requirements.

 Team Leadership & Functional Management 

 Lead, coach, and develop an agile marketing and communications team.

 Establish clear priorities, objectives, accountabilities, and development plans for team members.

 Foster collaboration across functions and ensure the team provides responsive, high-quality support to internal stakeholders.

 Manage the departmental operating budget and allocate resources according to business priorities.

 Select and manage external marketing, communications, creative, digital, media, and related service providers.

 Establish meaningful performance indicators and regularly report on results, risks, priorities, and resource requirements.

 Education 

 Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, Business Administration, Political Science, or a related field.

 A master's degree or relevant professional designation is considered an asset.

 Experience 

 Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in marketing and communications, including senior leadership accountability.

 Demonstrated experience leading internal and external communications, brand strategy, media relations, and integrated marketing initiatives.

 Proven experience leading and developing teams and managing cross-functional initiatives.

 Experience managing external agencies, consultants, contracts, budgets, and performance expectations.

 Experience overseeing Government Relations agencies, public affairs advisors, or stakeholder engagement programs is a strong asset.

 Experience in defence, government-facing, or a highly regulated industry is considered an asset.

 Skills, Knowledge & Behaviours 

 Strategic marketing and communications leadership.

 Brand stewardship and reputation management.

 Exceptional written, verbal, presentation, and executive communication skills.

 Strong agency governance, contract management, and budget oversight capabilities.

 Sound judgement and the ability to navigate sensitive, complex, or high-profile matters.

 Strong business acumen and ability to translate strategy into clear communication and marketing priorities.

 Executive presence and ability to advise and influence senior leaders.

 Effective people leadership, coaching, delegation, and prioritization.

 Strong project management and ability to lead multiple initiatives in a fast-paced environment.

 Collaborative, adaptable, creative, and results-oriented approach.

 Bilingualism in English and French, with strong English writing skills, is preferred.

 Working Conditions 

 Domestic and international travel required.

 Availability to support events, stakeholder engagements, or urgent communications outside regular business hours.

 Eligibility to obtain required security clearances and Controlled Goods access may be required.

 Security Clearance Requirements/ CGP / ITAR: 

 Position requires Controlled Goods Clearance and Level 2 Secret Clearance

 By joining Top Aces, you will find: 

 A work environment in which service, integrity, excellence and teamwork are highly valued;

 Opportunities for development and growth;

 Multidisciplinary and multicultural collaboration at a local and global level;

 A flexible schedule;

 Attractive benefit plan.

 Come share your passion with us! Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered, and challenged to be your best self.

 Equal Employment Opportunity 

 At Top Aces, all employees are welcome regardless of race, nationality, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, disability or age. The masculine form may be used in this job description solely for ease of reading but refers to men, women and gender diversity.

jobs.location: Canada; Dorval Head Office, Dorval, Quebec, Canada
jobs.description:
Founded in 2000 by three former Royal Canadian Air Force (RCAF) CF-18 fighter pilots who identified an opportunity to improve military readiness training, Top Aces has since established itself as the world leader in contracted adversary air (ADAIR) services and joint terminal attack controller (JTAC) training.

 We pride ourselves on our unblemished safety record, having flown an industry leading 130,000+ hours of operational training without accident in support of customers worldwide, including Canada, the U.S., Germany, and multiple other NATO allies and international partner nations.

 Our vision is to be the most trusted provider of innovative defense training solutions, continuously elevating standards in an industry where "Experience Matters." This commitment to innovation and technology ensures we remain adaptable, training allied militaries to succeed against evolving threats.

 Top Aces’ dynamic team contributes to delivering on our purpose of training the next generation of combat leaders by living our values of Service, Integrity, Excellence, and Together every day!

 Join our team!

 Position Summary 

 The Director of Data Management and Business Intelligence leads the enterprise data function for Top Aces. Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, the Director defines how data is governed, integrated, protected, and used across aviation operations, maintenance and engineering, supply chain, finance, safety, quality, human resources, commercial programs, and executive management.

 The role will establish trusted enterprise data products and decision-ready analytics while respecting aviation record integrity, contractual obligations, export controls, data residency, and need-to-know access. A central priority is to improve the quality and usability of data from Ramco and connected systems so that leaders and front-line teams can manage aircraft availability, maintenance execution, material readiness, program performance, and financial results with greater confidence.

 Top Aces Business Context 

 Top Aces provides advanced operational training and aircraft sustainment services to Canada, the United States, NATO members, and allied nations. The company operates globally in a safety-critical and security-sensitive environment that combines flight operations, maintenance and repair, engineering, supply chain, training, and proprietary technology. The data environment therefore requires strong governance across business units, legal entities, jurisdictions, and security domains.

 The Director will translate these operating realities into an enterprise data strategy that supports growth, operational readiness, regulatory compliance, and disciplined investment. The role must balance standardization with the access boundaries required for Canadian, U.S., and international programs.

 Key Responsibilities 

 Enterprise Data Strategy and Operating Model 

 Partner with the CIO to develop and execute a multi-year enterprise data and BI strategy aligned with Top Aces' business strategy, operating model, technology roadmap, and investment priorities.

 Create a practical data operating model that defines decision rights, ownership, stewardship, architecture standards, delivery methods, and support responsibilities across corporate and regional teams.

 Chair or support the enterprise data governance council and maintain a prioritized roadmap based on operational value, regulatory risk, data quality, and delivery capacity.

 Partner with the CIO and U.S. IT and security leadership to establish appropriate data segregation, access controls, and technology control plans for FOCI-related and export-controlled environments, where applicable.

 Data Governance Quality and Protection 

 Establish enterprise policies and standards for data ownership, classification, quality, lineage, retention, archival, residency, access, and acceptable use.

 Define authoritative sources and common business terms for critical domains, including aircraft, fleets, components, serialized parts, maintenance programs, work orders, defects, inventory, suppliers, customers, contracts, personnel, and financial dimensions.

 Implement data quality controls, issue-management workflows, and scorecards that identify root causes and assign corrective action to accountable data owners.

 Work with Cybersecurity, Legal, Export Compliance, Privacy, Quality, and program security personnel to protect personal, proprietary, controlled, and customer information throughout its lifecycle.

 Ensure analytics and data-sharing practices comply with applicable contractual clauses, the Canadian Controlled Goods Program, ITAR and EAR requirements, privacy laws, and customer security obligations.

 Data Architecture Integration and Platforms 

 Define the target enterprise data architecture, including ingestion, integration, master and reference data, lakehouse or warehouse services, semantic models, reporting, metadata, and monitoring.

 Establish integration patterns and data contracts for Ramco and other enterprise platforms using secure APIs, event-based interfaces, ETL or ELT pipelines, and controlled file exchange where required.

 Reduce duplicate datasets and spreadsheet-dependent reporting by creating reusable, governed data products and certified semantic models.

 Set engineering standards for observability, reconciliation, change control, testing, performance, resilience, backup, and recovery across the data platform.

 Manage the data-platform lifecycle, capacity, licensing, vendor performance, and total cost of ownership, with particular attention to Microsoft Fabric, Azure data services, Power BI, and connected technologies.

 Aviation and MRO Data 

 Lead data remediation and governance for Ramco MRO and ERP, focusing on master data, transactional integrity, usability, reporting structures, and interfaces with finance, supply chain, engineering, and flight operations.

 Partner with Maintenance, Engineering, Airworthiness, Quality, Supply Chain, and Operations to improve the completeness and consistency of aircraft configuration, component history, flight hours and cycles, maintenance plans, work packages, defects, technical records, and inventory data.

 Preserve the integrity and auditability of approved maintenance and airworthiness records while enabling controlled downstream analytics.

 Develop trusted measures for aircraft availability, dispatch reliability, mission-capable status, maintenance schedule compliance, turnaround time, component reliability, inventory availability, and aircraft-on-ground events.

 Support data readiness for operational and regulatory audits, customer reporting, contract performance reviews, and fleet-planning decisions.

 Business Intelligence and Performance Management 

 Lead the design and delivery of executive, operational, and functional dashboards using consistent definitions, clear ownership, and traceable data sources.

 Build an enterprise performance framework that connects mission delivery, safety, fleet readiness, maintenance, supply chain, program, customer, workforce, and financial measures.

 Develop governed self-service analytics so business users can answer routine questions without creating uncontrolled copies of sensitive data.

 Improve forecasting and scenario analysis for fleet utilization, maintenance demand, materials, labour capacity, contract delivery, revenue, cash flow, and program profitability.

 Maintain a transparent intake and prioritization process for BI requests, balancing regulatory deadlines, operational urgency, enterprise reuse, and expected value.

 Advanced Analytics and Artificial Intelligence 

 Identify and govern analytics and AI use cases such as predictive maintenance, component reliability, inventory optimization, demand forecasting, anomaly detection, and program risk monitoring.

 Require documented business ownership, suitable data quality, human oversight, security review, and measurable benefits before analytics or AI solutions move into production.

 Coordinate with engineering, operations, and technology teams when operational, training, mission-system, or live and synthetic data may be used, ensuring the work remains within approved classification and authorization boundaries.

 Monitor model performance, data drift, access, and business outcomes, and retire solutions that no longer meet operational, security, or financial requirements.

 Leadership and Stakeholder Partnership 

 Build and lead a capable team spanning data governance, architecture, engineering, BI, and analytics; define roles, develop talent, and manage succession for critical skills.

 Partner with executives and functional leaders to convert business questions into governed data products, clear measures, and practical decisions.

 Create an active network of business data owners and stewards and hold regular reviews of quality, adoption, access, and value realization.

 Manage external partners and vendors through clear outcomes, architecture standards, service levels, security requirements, and commercial accountability.

 Communicate data risks, progress, tradeoffs, and investment needs to senior leadership in concise business terms.

 Education and Experience 

 Bachelor's degree in computer science, information systems, data engineering, analytics, business, engineering, or a related discipline. A graduate degree or relevant professional certification is an asset.

 At least 10 years of progressive experience in data management, analytics, BI, enterprise applications, or data architecture, including at least five years leading teams or major cross-functional programs.

 Experience in aerospace, defense, aviation, MRO, or another highly regulated and asset-intensive industry is strongly preferred.

 Demonstrated experience improving data quality and reporting in a complex ERP or MRO environment. Direct experience with Ramco is a significant asset; experience with comparable aviation or enterprise platforms is also relevant.

 Experience operating across multiple countries, legal entities, or security domains, including Canada and the United States, is preferred.

 Technical and Regulatory Knowledge 

 Strong knowledge of enterprise data architecture, dimensional and semantic modelling, master data management, metadata, data quality, lineage, SQL, APIs, and ETL or ELT integration.

 Hands-on understanding of modern cloud data platforms and BI technologies. Experience with Microsoft Fabric, Azure, Power BI, and Microsoft data services is preferred.

 Working knowledge of aviation maintenance and supply-chain data, including serialized components, configuration, maintenance planning, technical records, reliability, and inventory transactions.

 Familiarity with aviation regulatory and quality environments such as Transport Canada, FAA, EASA, safety management systems, and AS9100 is an asset.

 Working knowledge of information classification, access control, auditability, privacy, data residency, the Canadian Controlled Goods Program, ITAR and EAR, CUI safeguards, CMMC, and NIST SP 800-171, as applicable to the role and programs supported.

 Ability to obtain and maintain the security clearances, controlled-goods eligibility, and customer or program authorizations required for the position.

 Leadership Competencies 

 Business judgment that connects data investment to safety, mission readiness, contract delivery, customer commitments, and financial performance.

 Ability to influence executives, operational leaders, technical specialists, and front-line users without relying solely on formal authority.

 Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain data limitations, security constraints, and architectural decisions to non-technical audiences.

 Disciplined program leadership, with practical experience managing priorities, budgets, vendors, risks, and organizational change.

 Commitment to Top Aces' values of Service, Integrity, Excellence, and Together.

 Professional fluency in English is required. French and additional languages used across Top Aces' operations are assets.

 Measures of Success 

 Annual objectives will be established with the CIO and business leaders. Measures should demonstrate stronger control of critical data and visible improvements in how the company operates and makes decisions.

 Security Clearance Requirements/ CGP / ITAR: 

 Position requires Level II clearance with the Canadian Government and the ability to gain access to the Canadian Controlled Goods Program.

 A work environment in which service, integrity, excellence and teamwork are highly valued;

 Opportunities for development and growth;

 Multidisciplinary and multicultural collaboration at a local and global level;

 A flexible schedule;

 Attractive benefit plan.

 Mimica is an AI-powered process intelligence platform enabling enterprises and individuals to reclaim their most precious resource: time.  Mimica automatically analyzes your team’s work, then generates the AI agents to execute it. Our software turns everyday work into data-backed decisions, helping companies remove process bottlenecks, automate the right tasks, and upskill teams with precision and confidence.
 We’ve raised $26 million in Series B financing and are scaling fast. Backed by investors including Khosla Ventures and Paladin Capital, our proprietary AI technology is trusted by Fortune 500 companies to accelerate transformation.  Our team 
 Behind our platform is a team of exceptionally talented people, remote-first and globally distributed across 16+ countries. We're looking for curious, collaborative people excited to solve complex problems. You'll join a fast-paced environment built on high ownership, bottom-up thinking, and transparent, open communication – helping some of the world's leading organizations transform the way work gets done with AI.

 Your mission 

 Mimica is growing fast, and so is the demand on our Platform Team. As Head of Platform, you will lead a lean but highly capable team that is the backbone of every engineering squad in the company, and you will own the infrastructure strategy, including all AI infrastructure, as we scale.
 The Platform team services the entire engineering organisation: keeping environments healthy, unblocking teams, building the infrastructure that lets everyone else move faster, and working with teams regarding SRE topics and developer experience too.  Familiarity with Crossplane, or a similar product like Config Connector.

 Experience with Temporal for workflow orchestration.
